models.name: DeepSeek-R1
models.notes: The flagship Chinese open-weight reasoning model; hosted by Microsoft Azure, Amazon Bedrock, and nearly every US inference provider. Also the SFT distillation teacher for NVIDIA's Llama-Nemotron family (2025, arXiv 2505.00949).

models.name: DeepSeek-V3.2
models.notes: V3.x line incl. V3.1 / V3.1-Terminus; on AWS Bedrock, SambaNova, W&B Inference (V3-0324).

models.name: DeepSeek-V4
models.notes: Current flagship line: on Azure AI Foundry (V4-Pro), Oracle OCI (imported V4 Flash/Pro), Together AI (V4-Flash-0731), Fireworks (Flash+Pro), W&B Inference (V4-Pro 1.6T MoE), OpenRouter (V4-Pro-0813). 2026-08: V4 Pro GA (DeepSWE 62.7% vs 12.8% preview; Terminal-Bench 2.1 87.9, level with Fable 5; Responses API + Codex CLI), 1.6T MoE / 49B active, 1M context; API price increase effective 2026-08-16; V4-Flash-0731 (2026-07-31) and V4-Flash-Vision-Exp (2026-08). V4-Flash-0731 also on Baseten, DeepInfra, and Ollama cloud (2026-08). Notably absent from Cerebras and AWS Bedrock as of 2026-08 OpenCode Zen (OpenCode's curated hosting service) serves V4 Pro + V4 Flash; Novita AI serves V4 Flash / V4-Flash-0731 / V4-Flash-Vision-Exp / V4-Pro / V4-Pro-0813 (2026-08) Perplexity self-hosts deepseek-v4-flash-0731 on its own Router API (2026-08) OpenRouter V4 census (2026-09-01): 17 providers each for V4 Pro and V4 Flash. US hosts: Baseten, CoreWeave, DeepInfra, DigitalOcean, Fireworks, GMICloud, Ionstream, NovitaAI, Parasail, Atlas Cloud, Azure (Microsoft), Venice; V4 Flash additionally on Cloudflare (and Mancer, unverified). New US hosts added to the graph: Atlas Cloud, GMI Cloud, ionstream, DigitalOcean, Parasail; new edges: CoreWeave, Cloudflare (Flash), Venice (Pro+Flash, from its own catalog). DeepSeek the company: first-ever external funding round — raising ~$7.4B (50B yuan) at a ~$74B valuation (WSJ 2026-08-27). OpenRouter V4 re-census (2026-09-02, endpoints API): V4-Flash-0731 now 29 provider endpoints (28 providers) and V4-Pro-0813 18 (17), up from 17 each at the 2026-09-01 census. New US hosting edges: Sail Research (Pro); AkashML, Makora, Morph, Wafer, and Relace (Flash — new company, San Francisco, YC W23, a16z-led $23M Series A). Skipped: OpenInference (Arize observability standard, not a verifiable inference company), Mancer 2 (unverified). EU-host census (2026-09-02): Inceptron (Lund, SE; V4-Flash FP4) and NextBit (Zaragoza, ES; V4-Flash + V4-Pro FP8, 100% renewable DC) now serve V4 on OpenRouter. V4-Flash-Vision-Exp (first experimental multimodal model in the V4 family; DeepSeek API 2026-08-21, open weights on HF 2026-08-31): built on the V4-Flash architecture + visual modules, 305B; multimodal-agent benchmarks leap (ApexBench 36.5 vs 26.2 for V4-Flash-0731, ALE 27.3 vs 25.2), text-agent parity (Terminal Bench 2.1: 83.9 vs 82.7; Opus-4.8: 85.0). OpenRouter endpoints (2026-09-02): Fireworks ($0.22/$0.66), Novita and DeepSeek first-party ($0.44/$1.32); also listed in Baseten’s model library (2026-09-02). 0813 GA checkpoint carries the DSpark speculative-decoding module (Together AI: “attached for faster generation”; official model card sglang example: --speculative-algorithm DSPARK). Nvidia published an NVFP4 quantization (nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813-NVFP4, HF 2026-09-01).

models.name: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B
models.notes: Chinese model distilled on top of a US (Meta Llama) base — a US company (Groq, Cerebras) hosting a Chinese distill of their own base.
models.disguise_note: Not a disguise, but a hybrid: R1 reasoning distilled onto a Meta base.

models.name: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B
models.notes: Chinese distill on a Chinese base; served in production on Cloudflare Workers AI.

models.name: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B
models.notes: Smallest R1-Distill variant (1.5B) — small enough for CPU deployment; Intel's official AWS Xeon deployment guide targets this size.

models.name: Qwen3 / Qwen2.5 family
models.notes: Qwen3 family on AWS Bedrock (with DeepSeek V3), Cloudflare (Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8), Groq (Qwen3-32B), Qualcomm AI Hub (on-device Qwen2-7B/Qwen3-4B), Hugging Face inference. Qwen3.5-9B served on Together AI serverless (2026).

models.name: Qwen3.8 27B
models.notes: Newest Qwen release; already on Cloudflare Workers AI and CoreWeave serverless (via OpenRouter) — Chinese open models ship to US production days after release. Qwen3.8 (2.4T, 2026-07-19) launched with open-weight commitment; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next variant (hybrid QSA attention) running NVFP4 on DGX Spark and unsloth GGUF (2026-08). Also served by Groq (qwen3.8-27b), Baseten, and Ollama cloud (12 variants, 256K, vision); lmstudio-community publishes MLX/GGUF builds Novita AI serves Qwen3.8 27B/Flash/Max; OpenCode Zen serves the Qwen3.5/3.6/3.7 Max+Plus API line. OpenRouter Qwen3.8-27B census (2026-09-01): 12 providers, 9 US-hosted — Reka, AkashML, Parasail, CoreWeave, NovitaAI, Venice, Ionstream, Cloudflare, io.net (Chutes unverified; Alibaba and Phala are the non-US rows). New edges: Reka, Venice (from its own catalog), plus the new companies AkashML, Ionstream, Parasail, io.net. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next open-weights release (2026-08-26): multimodal MoE, 125B+ total / 6B active per token — first open model built on the architecture that will underpin Qwen4 (Ollama, Hugging Face). Qwen3.8-Max-0902 (2026-09-02): API refresh of the Max-class flagship; Max-class weights not yet released (r/LocalLLaMA 2026-09-02).

models.name: Kimi K2.6 (Moonshot AI)
models.notes: Moonshot's Kimi line. DoorDash (US F500) tested/used K2.6 on its codebase (2026 House inquiry). Served by Baseten (HF Inference), detected in Microsoft's own stack, served on OpenRouter. Also: Cerebras Dedicated Endpoints (2026-04-27), DeepInfra Also on OpenCode Zen (K2.5/K2.6) and Novita AI (2026-08) OpenRouter K2.6 census (2026-09-02, endpoints API): 21 provider endpoints. US hosts: Decart, CoreWeave, Crusoe (new company), DeepInfra, Venice, Parasail, GMI Cloud, DigitalOcean, Cloudflare, Atlas Cloud, Baseten, Fireworks, Novita (+ OpenRouter host of record). Non-US: Moonshot, Baidu, SiliconFlow; excluded: Chutes, StreamLake, Inceptron, Phala (no verifiable US footprint). K2.6 now has a US hosting layer on par with K3. + Inceptron (Lund, SE; INT4) as an OpenRouter host (2026-09-02).

models.name: Kimi K3
models.notes: World's first open 3T-class model (blog 2026-07-14; all 2.8T weights on Hugging Face 2026-07-26, 96 shards, bespoke Kimi K3 License): 2.8T-parameter MoE (104B active), Kimi Delta Attention (hybrid linear attention), native vision, 1M context. Tops Frontend Code Arena at 1679 (Claude Fable 5: 1631, GPT-5.6 Sol: 1618). Day-0 hosting: Together AI and Modal; expanded to Baseten, DeepInfra, Ollama cloud, and GitHub Copilot (GA 2026-08-06, $3/$15 per M tokens, 'frontier-level agentic coding at highly cost-effective pricing'). Also in Cursor (2026-07-27), NVIDIA NIM and Fireworks. Base of Harvey Tenet (post-training, 2026-08). Reuters 2026-08-26: Moonshot in talks with Azure/AWS/Google Cloud over K3 hosting (up to 30% revenue share) Also on OpenCode Zen ($3/$15 per M) and Novita AI Perplexity self-hosts Kimi K3 on its Router API ($3/$15 per M) Fireworks Serverless Training offers Multi-LoRA training + serving on K3 (private preview, 2026-07-26) Digital Applied provider census (2026-08-31) adds US K3 hosts: Cloudflare (docs: 1M ctx, $3.00/M input — the census's 1.31M figure is a 1,048,576+262,144 sum artifact), Makora ($2.55/$12.75, cheapest of 17), Reka (fp8), Sail Research (fp4), Venice ($1.75/$5.50, cheapest endpoint). Groq does NOT list K3/GLM-5.3/V4 (lists MiniMax-M2.7 + Qwen3.x dense). OpenRouter K3 census (2026-09-01): 18 provider rows in the us region, incl. new US hosts Morph (+Morph Fast), Wafer, Parasail and DigitalOcean. Correction: Cloudflare, Reka and Venice do NOT host K3 on OpenRouter — the 2026-08-31 census rows attributed to K3 were GLM-5.3 endpoints (Venice's K3 is $3.75/$18.75 per its own catalog; the census $1.75/$5.50 is its GLM-5.3 price). POLICY (2026-07-22): White House OSTP Director Michael Kratsios (X): "We have information that Moonshot AI distilled Anthropic's Fable for the development of its K3 model" (also alleged restricted Nvidia chips) — no public evidence offered; independent timeline analyses (2026-07-22/26) find it unproven. Treasury Secretary Bessent (X, 2026-07-22): "Open source is not open season on American IP" — when firms conduct "covert, industrial-scale distillation attacks that cross the line into IP theft, sanctions and Entity List designations will be on the table". COMMERCIAL: Moonshot in talks with Microsoft, Amazon and Google over hosting K3 with up to 30% revenue share (Reuters 2026-08-26; see edges c173/c174, not yet live). K3 License commercial clause (reported 2026-07-16, release data v18): MaaS businesses with >$20M total annual revenue must enter a separate agreement with Moonshot before commercial use — the license-level complement to the cloud revenue-share talks. COMPUTE (2026-07-20): Moonshot paused new Kimi K3 subscriptions after launch demand pushed GPU capacity near its ceiling (official Kimi X post; TechNode first to report). US-hyperscaler surfaces added 2026-07/08: Microsoft Foundry via Fireworks (2026-07-28), official AWS deployment guide on SageMaker HyperPod/EKS (2026-07-30), Databricks US-hosting on its Foundation Model API via Unity AI Gateway (2026-08-06, edge c369).

models.name: GLM-5 (GLM-5.2/5.3)
models.notes: GLM-5 line. GLM-5.3 (2026-08-14; open weights 2026-08-28, zai-org/GLM-5.3 on HF): SOTA on Terminal-Bench 3.0 + CyberGym; +50% coding vs GLM-5.2 on Z.ai Code Bench; 744B-class MoE, 1M context. GLM-5.3-Flash (2026-08-26, 320B MoE / 18B active, multimodal): ran free as stealth 'ox-alpha' on OpenRouter/OpenCode for ~a week before being named. Hosting: Together AI, OpenRouter, Baseten (5.2/5.3/Flash), DeepInfra (5/5.1/5.2/5.3-Flash), Ollama cloud (US/EU), Cerebras Dedicated Endpoints (GLM 5/5.1, 2026-04-27), HF Inference. Tooling: Red Hat AI NVFP4, Unsloth GGUF, Z.ai ZCode harness OpenCode Zen serves GLM 5/5.1/5.2; Novita AI serves GLM 5/5.1/5.2/5.3/5.3-Flash (2026-08) Perplexity self-hosts GLM-5.2/5.3 on its Router API (2026-08) OpenRouter GLM-5.3 census (2026-09-01): 24 providers, 20 US-hosted — Together, Baseten, DeepInfra, Fireworks, Makora, Modal, Sail Research, NovitaAI plus Reka, AkashML, io.net, Morph, Friendli, Cloudflare, GMICloud, Parasail, DigitalOcean, Decart, Wafer and Venice. Also confirmed on Reka's OpenRouter provider page (GLM-5.3 + Flash; the source of the 2026-08-31 census misattribution). OpenRouter GLM-5.2 census (2026-09-02, endpoints API): 34 provider endpoints. New US edge: Sail Research ($0.50/$3.15 per M). Confirmed US hosts: Novita, DeepInfra, Decart, DigitalOcean, CoreWeave, Atlas Cloud, GMI Cloud, Reka, Baseten, Fireworks, Cloudflare, Parasail, Together, Venice, Friendli, Crusoe. Non-US rows: Baidu, Z.AI, Alibaba, SiliconFlow, Mistral (EU). Excluded: StreamLake, Inceptron, Phala. EU hosts confirmed 2026-09-02 (endpoints API): Mistral AI (GLM-5.2), Inceptron (GLM-5.2 + GLM-5.3, FP4), NextBit (GLM-5.3-Flash, FP8). Ox Alpha week (2026-08-20→27): Z.ai claims the ENTIRE free-preview traffic was served on a cluster of ~100,000 Chinese-made AI chips, no NVIDIA hardware (CNBC 2026-08-27; stock +8%) — the first frontier-class open-model week served wholly on domestic Chinese silicon; Bloomberg (2026-08-26): Ox Alpha 'rivals DeepSeek'.

models.notes: The reference US open model: usage 'doubled' May-Jul 2024; Goldman Sachs GS AI Platform (2024-08), Wells Fargo open-source LLM apps (2024); base for DeepSeek's R1 distill and Hermes 4. Llama 4 shipped in 2026.

models.name: SWE-1.5
models.notes: Cognition's fast SWE agent model (2x faster than GPT-5, 950 tok/s on Cerebras). Closed model served in Windsurf — no public weights.

models.name: GPT family (4o, 5.x / Codex)
models.notes: The default closed frontier: JPMorgan LLM Suite, Visa partnership, T-Mobile, Uber, Salesforce (Agentforce default), Sierra, Notion, Figma-era stack, Anduril, Palantir AIP. 2026: GPT-5.5 (2026-04-23, +Pro/Instant) and GPT-5.6 Sol (Arena 1618).

models.name: Claude family (Sonnet/Opus 4.x-5, Fable 5.1, Mythos 5.1)
models.notes: Second closed frontier: BofA 'all in' (2026), ServiceNow multi-year, Adobe Firefly Assistant, Cognition/Devin, Sierra, Vercel v0, Figmalog, JPMorgan. 2026: Sonnet 5 (2026-06-30), Opus 5 (2026-07-24); Fable 5 is Anthropic's frontier flagship (Frontend Code Arena 1631). IPO baseline reportedly above $1T for an October 2026 debut (FutureX, 2026-09). 2026-09-01: Fable 5.1 (general API; Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise) and Mythos 5.1 (trusted access only), both $10/$50, 75% cheaper Fable cache reads (VentureBeat).

models.name: Gemini family
models.notes: Third closed frontier: CVS Health platform, Lowe's Mylow, Home Depot agentic tools, Sierra, Wells Fargo Fargo assistant (Dialogflow/PaLM lineage).

models.name: Grok family (4.x)
models.notes: xAI frontier (X ecosystem). No Chinese-model edge found. Grok 4.6 (2026-08-12, SpaceX AI): half-frontier pricing, double included usage in Cursor during launch week.

models.name: Apple Foundation Models
models.notes: Apple's on-device LLMs (Apple Intelligence). WWDC26 'Core AI' additionally ships pre-converted open-weight models (Qwen, Mistral) for on-device inference.

models.name: Palmyra family
models.notes: Writer's in-house open-weight enterprise models; also distributed via AWS Bedrock.

models.name: Birdbrain
models.notes: Duolingo's in-house model system (est. 2020).

models.name: Firefly
models.notes: Adobe's in-house image models; Firefly Assistant (2026-04) adds Claude on top.

models.name: Magic Apron
models.notes: Home Depot's proprietary generative AI suite (press release, 2025-03-06).

models.notes: Mastercard's in-house next-gen generative AI engine (2026 story).

models.notes: Suno's in-house music generation models.

models.name: Runway Gen-4

models.name: Midjourney v6/v7
models.notes: Midjourney's in-house image models.

models.name: ElevenLabs TTS/voice models
models.notes: ElevenLabs' in-house speech models (incl. enterprise 'in-house' variants).

models.name: v0-1.x (composite)
models.notes: Vercel's v0 composite model family; 'currently uses Anthropic's Sonnet 3.7, v0-1.5 uses Sonnet 4' (official blog).

models.name: AT&T fine-tuned SLMs
models.notes: AT&T fine-tuned small models (NVIDIA NeMo workflow) for code review & call center; ~84% cost cut reported. Base family not named in sources found.

models.name: DeepSeek-R1-Qwen-7B (Baseten)
models.notes: A US company's model fine-tuned from a Chinese base with Chinese (DeepSeek R1) chain-of-thought — the cleanest example of Chinese open-weight DNA inside a US product.

models.name: (undisclosed LLM)
models.notes: Placeholder node for productions where the company confirms LLM/AI usage but does not name the model (Comcast AMA, Airbnb assistant, Netflix serving, Harvey open-source fine-tune base, Perplexity in-house, Wayve Wayformer, Abridge).

models.name: Wayformer / Wayve AV foundation model
models.arch: end-to-end embodied-AV foundation model; GAIA generative driving world model
models.notes: Wayve's in-house end-to-end autonomous-driving foundation model (Wayve AI Driver / AV2.0) and the GAIA generative driving world model (2023). Built in-house; no Chinese open-weight lineage.

models.name: MiniMax M3
models.notes: MiniMax M3 (2026-06-01): first open-weights model to combine frontier coding, 1M context and native multimodality. One of OpenRouter's four 'open-weight models that matter' in June 2026 ('MiniMax owns multimodal-on-a-budget', AA index 44). Eclipsed GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro on key benchmarks at 5-10% of the cost ($0.60/$2.40 per M tokens, VentureBeat 2026-06-01). Also on DeepInfra (full M2→M3 family, 2026-08) OpenCode Zen serves M3/M2.7/M2.5; Novita AI serves the full M1→M3 line (2026-08) SambaCloud (MiniMax M3 + M2.7, 2026-09) OpenRouter M3 census (2026-09-02, endpoints API): 11 provider endpoints. US hosts: CoreWeave, DeepInfra, Atlas Cloud, Parasail, Novita, Venice, SambaNova, GMI Cloud. Non-US: Minimax; excluded: StreamLake, ModelRun. (Fireworks and Together keep their earlier high-confidence edges; both no longer appear in the current listing.) + ModelRun/Modular (FP4) as an OpenRouter host (2026-09-02; Modular in Qualcomm acquisition, announced 2026-06-24).

models.name: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
models.notes: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra (2026): the strongest US open-weight entrant - 'the clearest sign that strong open-weight models are not just coming from Chinese labs' (OpenRouter, June 2026). Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.1: 48 (vs GLM-5.2 51, MiniMax M3 44, DeepSeek V4 Pro 44). Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (2026-08-11): open 30B MoE (3B active) for the high-volume agent execution layer; on OpenRouter, Ollama, NVIDIA NIM (NVFP4). Nemotron 4 family in development (largest planned model ≥1T params; The Information).

models.name: Kimi K2.5 (Moonshot AI)
models.notes: Kimi K2.5 - K2-series predecessor to K2.6/K3. Notably the undisclosed base of Anysphere's (Cursor) Composer 2 (TechCrunch, 2026-03-22), delivered through a commercial partnership with Fireworks AI. Also offered in Windsurf/Devin Desktop (2026-04).

models.name: Cursor Composer 2 (Anysphere)
models.notes: DISGUISE CASE: Anysphere's in-house coding model built on top of Moonshot's Kimi K2.5 'without disclosing this fact anywhere in its initial announcement' (TechCrunch, 2026-03-22). Kimi's official account called it a 'legitimate commercial partnership' conducted through Fireworks AI; Cursor co-founder Aman Sanger: 'It was a mistake not to state from the outset in our blog post that it was Kimi-based.'

models.name: Kimi K2.7 Code
models.notes: Moonshot's open-weight coding model (K2.7-Code). First open-weight model offered as a selectable option in GitHub Copilot: GA 2026-07-01 (Pro/Pro+/Max), Business/Enterprise 2026-07-07. Day-1 hosting: Together AI, Baseten, DeepInfra; also on OpenRouter. 'May be less aligned than other Copilot models' (GitHub docs) Also on OpenCode Zen and Novita AI (2026-08) OpenRouter K2.7-Code census (2026-09-02, endpoints API): 16 provider endpoints. US hosts: DeepInfra, CoreWeave, Venice, GMI Cloud, Cloudflare, Baseten, Together (+ OpenRouter host of record). Non-US: Moonshot, Alibaba; excluded: Inceptron, StreamLake, ModelRun (CN). + Inceptron (INT4) and ModelRun/Modular (FP4) as OpenRouter hosts (2026-09-02).

models.name: Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B
models.notes: Qwen3.8 flagship open-weight variant: 2.4T-parameter MoE, 95B active (A95B), text-only with mandatory thinking mode (no multimodal, thinking cannot be disabled). Weights on Hugging Face 2026-08-12; Qwen3.8-Max blog 2026-08-02 ('A New Bar for Coding and Cowork'). OpenRouter day-1 (qwen3.8-2.4t-a95b); also on DeepInfra and Together AI Novita AI (Qwen3.8 2.4T A95B, 2026-08) Qwen3.8-Max-0902 dated snapshot released 2026-09-01: same 2.4T/A95B base + 1M context, further post-trained on coding/office/agents/vision, same price (OpenRouter: qwen/qwen3.8-max). OpenRouter 2.4T census (2026-09-02, endpoints API): 7 provider endpoints. US hosts: DeepInfra, Modal, Novita, Together, Venice ($2.00/$6.00 per M, most at 1M ctx). Non-US: Alibaba, SiliconFlow.

models.name: MiniMax M2.7
models.notes: MiniMax M2.7 (2026-03-18): agentic coding model with "self-evolution" — autonomously debugs and optimizes its own training pipeline, reportedly handling 30-50% of its own development workflow. Frontier-adjacent coding/reasoning at a fraction of frontier cost. Served on Groq (catalog, 2026-08-31), OpenCode Zen, SambaCloud, DeepInfra. OpenRouter M2.7 census (2026-09-02, endpoints API): 10 provider endpoints. US hosts: MARA Holdings (new company; cloud.mara.com inference API, North Central TX racks), DeepInfra, Novita, Atlas Cloud, GMI Cloud, Groq, SambaNova (+ OpenRouter host of record).

models.name: Magistral Medium

models.name: Mixtral 8x7B

Successor to Hy3 (295B/21B, Apache 2.0). Tuned for coding, research and financial analysis. OpenRouter listing 2026-08-28 ($0.834/$2.501 per M, 1048k ctx); launch provider Tencent Cloud.

models.name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
models.notes: Open-weights flash variant of Qwen3.8 (2026-08-26): multimodal MoE, 125B+ total / 6B active per token, hybrid QSA attention - first open model built on the architecture that will underpin Qwen4 (HF tag 'qwen4_exp'). Official repo Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Qwen open-weights license); Ollama library + community GGUF (NVFP4 on DGX Spark). OpenRouter qwen/qwen3.8-flash since 2026-08-26 (1M ctx, $0.15/$0.47 per M, multimodal reasoning); also on Novita AI (2026-08 catalog). OpenRouter endpoints API (2026-09-02) lists only the Alibaba endpoint for qwen/qwen3.8-flash; the OpenRouter and Novita edges are kept (Novita continues via its own catalog — 02l convention).

models.name: Polaris (Hippocratic AI)
models.arch: safety-focused LLM "constellation": stateful primary agent + specialist support agents (ensemble of multi-billion-parameter LLMs, ~1T constellation)
models.notes: Hippocratic AI’s healthcare-specialized voice agent. Polaris 1 (arXiv 2403.13313, 2024-03-20): first safety-focused LLM constellation for real-time patient–AI conversations, co-trained on proprietary clinical data; outperformed GPT-4 and LLaMA-2-70B (used as evaluation baselines, not components). Polaris 5.0 (2026-04-30): built on 180M+ real patient interactions; frontier models (GPT-5.4 Pro, Claude Opus 4.7, Gemini 3.1 Pro) appear as benchmark reference points only.

models.name: π0 (Physical Intelligence)
models.arch: vision-language-action (VLA) flow-matching robot foundation model (PaliGemma 3B VLM backbone + flow-matching action expert)
models.notes: General-purpose robotic foundation model (laundry folding, table cleaning, box assembly …). Open-sourced as openpi (code + weights, Apache-2.0, ~13.6k stars) so anyone can fine-tune it to their own robots. Not an LLM — a VLA; included as a notable US open-weights model. Successor π0.7 (2026-04) is in-house.

models.name: Qwen3.5 (397B-A17B)
models.arch: MoE LLM, 397B total / 17B active, native vision (image + video), 1M context
models.notes: First open-weights model in the Qwen3.5 series (Alibaba, 2026-02-16; HF LICENSE file dated Feb 16; CNBC 2026-02-26: "Alibaba unveils Qwen3.5 as China's chatbot race shifts to AI agents"). Base of Thomson Reuters' in-house Thomson-1 via the "Snowdon" adaptation (see disguise_cases).

models.name: Thomson-1 (Thomson Reuters)
models.arch: legal-domain LLM (continual learning on the Qwen3.5-based "Snowdon" adaptation)
models.notes: DISGUISE CASE: Thomson Reuters' first proprietary LLM ($40m talent + compute). The official announcement describes the base only as "a strong open-source foundation" (unnamed); CTO Joel Hron named it in an interview (Business Insider, 2026-08-24): "Snowdon" — an Alibaba Qwen model (identified by BI as Qwen3.5) "realigning"-adapted over several months by a Thomson Reuters + Imperial College team, "ethically and politically de-biased and safe to use". "There's nothing that necessarily ties us to Qwen" (Hron). Deploys in CoCounsel Legal's high-volume document review (previously Claude). TR technical report (2026-08-17) benchmarks Thomson-1.0-Large against "Qwen 3.5 397B" (its base) and frontier models; "on par with the latest frontier models" (CEO Hasker, company-eval).

models.name: Harvey Tenet
models.notes: DISGUISE CASE (disclosed at launch): Harvey's first proprietary legal model — "a Kimi K3 base that we post-trained together with Fireworks research for long-horizon legal work" (Harvey blog, 2026-08-20, research preview). All-pass rate ~11% (base K3) → 19.7% (Tenet); claimed to outperform both the base model and US frontier systems (Fable 5, GPT-5.6 Sol) on complex legal agentic tasks (Fortune, 2026-08-27). Unlike Composer 2 / Thomson-1, the Chinese base was stated in the launch post itself.

models.name: Inkling (Thinking Machines)
models.arch: MoE LLM, 975B total / 41B active, multimodal (image + text + audio), 1M context; Inkling-Small 276B/12B variant
models.notes: Thinking Machines' first model trained from scratch with full open weights (2026-07-15) — the leading US open-weights model (debuting at 41 on the AA Intelligence Index; "#1 US open weight" per r/LocalLLaMA, 2026-08-02). Trained from scratch on 45T tokens (text/image/audio/video) — explicitly NOT a Chinese-base model; the US counterpoint to Qwen3.5 / Kimi K3 / GLM-5.2. Day-0 support: transformers, SGLang, vLLM, llama.cpp.

models.name: Meta Muse Spark
models.arch: frontier multimodal reasoning MoE (~10T params reported)
models.notes: Meta's flagship closed model, launched 2026-04-08 (Meta's first proprietary model; ~10T parameters per Musk's post). Spark 1.1 July 2026; Spark 1.2 + Muse Code (beta) early Aug 2026 (Zuckerberg: 1.2 weights will be open-sourced); Spark 1.3 released 2026-09-02 with roadmap line 'the Muse Spark open weights release ... Stay tuned' (Meta AI Research). Rollout day (2026-09-02): Zuckerberg 'rolling out today… Next up 🍉' (X); press: 'frontier performance,' claims top DeepSWE score (Techmeme 2026-09-02). Official (Meta research blog + AIatMeta, 2026-09-02): live in Muse Code + Meta Model API; claims top DeepSWE 1.1 score over GPT-5.6 / Opus 5 (75.4%; long-context 98.5%; independent verification pending); ~20% fewer tool calls / ~25% fewer tokens vs 1.2 (Meta engineer comparisons). Source of Muse Glimmer (distilled). No US enterprise hosting recorded (AWS Bedrock only, per 2026-08-10 registry doc).

models.name: Meta Muse Glimmer
models.notes: 30B open agentic model from Meta Superintelligence Labs (2026-08-10), Apache 2.0 — 'a more permissive license than Llama ever carried' (VentureBeat). Optimized for always-on local agent workflows (local agents, function calling, local coding, LLM-as-a-judge); runs on a Mac/PC single consumer GPU. 'Developed in part from' closed Muse Spark (The Hindu 2026-08-11; S. Raschka 2026-08-13: distilled). Open weights on Hugging Face; local via Ollama. No US enterprise hosting as of 2026-09-02 (AWS Bedrock only, per 2026-08-10 registry doc).
